description: A widely prescribed penicillin-type (beta-lactam) antibiotic for common bacterial infections of the ear, chest, throat, and urinary tract. It kills bacteria by disrupting their cell-wall synthesis.

halfLife.conditions: healthy adults; label states an elimination half-life of 61.3 minutes (~1.0 h)

vd.conditions: apparent volume of distribution ~0.3–0.4 L/kg (SmPC); point value 0.35 L/kg reproduces the label's 500 mg oral peak (~5.5–7.5 µg/mL) under this one-compartment fit. Scaled to absolute litres against the 70 kg reference subject at derivation time.

F.conditions: SmPC states amoxicillin is approximately 70% orally bioavailable; other sources report up to ~89% for doses ≤ 2 g. Absorption is not affected by food.

tmax.conditions: peak blood levels 1–2 h after oral administration (label); SmPC median ~1 h. Point value 1 h. Note ke (from a ~1 h half-life) is close to ka here, so this drug sits near the ka≈ke absorption/elimination boundary.

validation.conditions: 500 mg capsule: 'average peak blood levels 1 to 2 hours after administration in the range of ... 5.5 mcg/mL to 7.5 mcg/mL' (food state not stated for the capsules). NOT an independent check: Vd 0.35 L/kg was chosen to reproduce this peak, so this entry only guards it against later edits. The model lands inside the range, near its top

250 mg capsule: average peak blood levels 'in the range of 3.5 mcg/mL to 5 mcg/mL', same label sentence as the 500 mg entry. The model lands inside the range, near its bottom; since the model is linear it is the 500 mg fit halved, so this mainly checks that the label's two capsule ranges are mutually dose-proportional

875 mg TABLET, single-dose crossover bioequivalence study in 27 adults, dosed at the start of a light meal after an overnight fast: Cmax 13.8 +/- 4.1 mcg/mL (AUC 35.4 +/- 8.1 mcg.h/mL). The most independent of the three: a different study, formulation and dose from the capsule peak the volume was chosen against. The model reads ~8% low

fda_label.title: Amoxicillin Capsule (NorthStar Rx LLC; mfr Aurobindo Pharma) — FDA Structured Product Label, clinical pharmacology (half-life, Tmax, peak levels, protein binding; 250/500 mg capsule average peak blood levels 3.5–5 and 5.5–7.5 mcg/mL; 875 mg tablet Cmax 13.8 ± 4.1 mcg/mL in a 27-adult bioequivalence study)

smpc.title: Amoxicillin 500 mg Capsules — Summary of Product Characteristics (emc), section 5.2 pharmacokinetic properties (bioavailability, volume of distribution)

notes: Curated from the FDA Structured Product Label for amoxicillin capsules (NorthStar/Aurobindo — half-life 61.3 min, Tmax 1–2 h, 250/500 mg peak blood levels, ~20% protein binding) plus the EMA SmPC (medicines.org.uk) for the apparent volume of distribution (~0.3–0.4 L/kg) and oral bioavailability (~70%), which the US label does not quantify. ke is taken from the ~1 h half-life. Amoxicillin is US oral-only (its IV sibling is ampicillin), so only the oral route is offered. LINEARITY: within 250–3000 mg the bioavailability (AUC) is proportional to dose and elimination is first-order and renal (dose-independent half-life), so identical repeated doses superpose and linear: true. The one documented nonlinearity is in the absorption RATE, not in AUC or elimination: at higher single doses the absorption rate saturates, which flattens Cmax (sub-proportional) and pushes Tmax later. That means the single ka used here is valid for the illustrative dose but would overstate the absorption rate at much larger doses — a shape caveat, not a superposition-breaking nonlinearity. A curatorial cross-check: Vd 0.35 L/kg with F 0.70 lands the 500 mg peak (7.25 µg/mL) inside the label's reported 5.5–7.5 µg/mL range under this one-compartment model, which is why that Vd point value was chosen within the 0.3–0.4 range. Because the volume was fitted to it, that 500 mg peak is a regression guard, not evidence. The independent check is the label's 875 mg tablet study (Cmax 13.8 ± 4.1 mcg/mL in 27 adults): the model gives 12.7, ~8% low, and its AUC (~37 mcg·h/mL against 35.4) agrees too. All three anchors are encoded in `validation`. Because the half-life (~1 h) makes ke comparable to the absorption rate ka, amoxicillin is a good illustration of near-flip-flop kinetics. Educational illustration only — not for dosing.
